findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Employees were observed on their phone and donning gloves right after without handwashing. Education was carried out. The behavior was corrected. Ensure that employees stay off their phone and always wash their hands before donning gloves at all times.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer within the sani buckets were reading at 0ppm during the inspection. Education was carried out. A staff member remade the sani buckets and they tested at 200 ppm. Ensure that sanitizer concentration are frequently checked to maintain appropriate sanitation of food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1) Inspector observed raw chicken being stored above raw shell eggs in the walk-in cooler. PIC was made aware. PIC removed the raw chicken and stored it appropriately. Ensure that proper storage order is observed at all times to avoid cross contamination of food items. 

Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.

Discussed with PIC and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff are aware that they need to wash their hands whenever they change tasks.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.comment:

findings.comment:
2-301.12: During the inspection, it was observed that an employee failed to utilize a barrier when turning off the water at the hand sink, thus re-contaminating their hands. This action was corrected with education provided as to why the barrier is an important step in the hand washing process. Ensure proper training is accomplished for all employees on how to properly wash hands from start to finish.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Many areas in the facility are in need of a general cleaning. These areas include, but are not limited to, shelving, counters, and tabletops in the facility. Ensure these areas are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency that prevents the accumulation of soil residue and debris.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The facility is in need of a general and deep cleaning of floors and other various hard to reach surfaces behind equipment. Ensure cleaning takes place at a frequency to prevent soil and debris accumulation.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The fridge under the sliding door cooler by the single service items was observed to leak water. This water is being caught by two pans under the doors. Ensure this equipment is repaired or discarded to prevent the water leaking.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The hand sink by the single service items is in need of caulking where the metal meets the wall. Ensure this area is sealed to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface where debris and other residues are unable to accumulate.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: 2-301.14: Employee was observed to exit the facility and reenter and immediately resume their assigned duties without washing their hands. This behavior was ceased immediately by the inspector and employee was requested to wash their hands. Inspector spoke with PIC to ensure reminders and proper training are reinforced with the staff.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: The baffle, the plastic piece in the ice machine, was observed to be visibly soiled with what appears to be mold growth or another foreign type substance. PIC was made aware of this and cleaning/sanitizing of the baffle is taking place during the time of inspection. Ensure this baffle is regularly cleaned and sanitized to prevent growth of foreign substances and to maintain the integrity of the safety of the ice.
4-602.11: (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: The meat and chili on the hot holding prep table registered at temperatures below the required 135 degrees F for hot holding. The meat, when probed, registered at 100 degrees F and had been in place since 10am this day. This container was disposed of and replaced with a fresh container of meat. The chili, when probed, registered at 123 degrees F and was in place at 1pm. Using time instead of temperature, the facility must dispose of the chili in the container at 5pm to ensure its food safety integrity. If this steam table is to have continued use, then the establishment must maintain a time control log where the food is replaced every 4 hours or the steam table needs to be turned up in temperature or maintenance needs to be requested for the equipment to be fixed or replaced. The facility is going to be using a controlled substance, more than likely a pan of water, to test the temperature availability of the steam table and to better gauge if they need it fixed, replaced, or simply turned up in temperature.
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: The ice scoop at the drive thru was observed to be stored with the scoop inside the ice machine where the handle was in contact with the ice. The scoop was removed and education was given to the drive thru worker at the time that this practice is unacceptable. Ensure that staff is trained on all proper storage methods that prevents contamination of food items and that the ice scoop is stored properly.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The caulking by the double sink in the back and by the grill on the prep table appears to be soiled and degrading. Ensure this caulking is removed from these locations and is replaced with fresh caulk in a manner that makes a good seal with the wall and allows the material to be smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.
